unit: Unit 13: Making Your Computer Easier to Use
title: Now adjust your own computer
drDigitalIntro:
You have moved every one of these settings on a practice machine. Now move them where they count.
• You will zoom this page in and back out, and the page reads the real zoom level as you do it.
• You will turn on Reduce Motion in your computer's own settings, and this page will see it change, because your browser passes that preference on to every website.
• Then the ones only you can judge: text size, pointer size, and the screen reader.
• Nothing here is a commitment. Every setting in this mission goes back exactly the way it came.

playgroundTask.goal: You set up your own computer the way it suits you

steps.say: Zoom this page in past 120 per cent, then put it back to 100.
steps.detail: Hold Ctrl, or Command on a Mac, and press the + key. Ctrl and 0 puts it back. This changes one website's size and nothing else — which is exactly what you want when only one site sets its text too small.

steps.say: Turn Reduce Motion on in your computer's own settings.
steps.detail: It is in the accessibility section of Settings. It stops windows sliding and screens sweeping about, which helps a lot of people and is worth trying even if you have never thought about it.

steps.say: Make the text bigger everywhere, not just on one page.
steps.detail: This is a system setting, not a browser one — it changes menus, buttons and labels across every app. Bigger text means less fits on screen, which is a trade worth making if you are squinting.

steps.say: Make the pointer bigger until you can find it without hunting.
steps.detail: Losing the pointer is not a failing of yours; the default is small. There is also a setting that makes it grow when you shake the mouse.

steps.say: Turn the screen reader on for one minute, then turn it off.
steps.detail: It reads aloud whatever you point at. One minute is enough to understand how somebody who cannot see the screen uses the same computer you do.

drDigitalSuccess: Every one of those was on your own machine, and two of them this page could see for itself.
drDigitalHint: For Reduce Motion, look in the accessibility part of Settings — it is usually under a heading about motion or animation. The box updates the moment you switch it.
warning: The screen reader takes over the keyboard while it is on. To turn it off again: on a Mac hold Command and press F5; on Windows hold the Windows key and Ctrl and press Enter.
